subject: economics
title: Public Goods and Information
welcome_lead: When the market cannot supply at all - or supplies based on bad data.
meta_desc: A-Level Market Failure: public goods and asymmetric information.
final_note: Public goods, free rider problems and information failures all justify intervention.

concepts.def: Free market produces an allocation that is not Pareto efficient; sources include externalities, public goods, information failure.
Where price diverges from marginal social cost; creates deadweight loss.
Akerlof (1970) Market for Lemons: used car buyers know less than sellers, causing market unravelling.
Insured parties take more risk because they don't bear full costs; explains 2008 banking crisis behaviour.
Low-quality buyers/sellers crowd out high-quality due to information asymmetry; insurance markets vulnerable.
Goods with positive externalities under-consumed by free market; e.g. vaccines, education.

walkthroughs.body_html: If a good is non-excludable, sellers cannot charge - free riders consume free. If it is non-rival, marginal cost is zero. Private supply collapses; government usually steps in.
Used-car sellers know more than buyers; insurers know less than the insured. Both adverse selection and moral hazard can collapse markets if no signalling or screening is possible.
Government can provide public goods directly. For information failures: regulate disclosure, require licences, mandate insurance pools, or run public information campaigns.
